portal_description:
The cyrus-sasl packages contain the Cyrus implementation of Simple Authentication and Security Layer (SASL). SASL is a method for adding authentication support to connection-based protocols.

This update fixes the following bugs:

*  Previously, unnecessary quote characters were used in the cyrus-sasl.spec file when the user was created using the useradd command. Consequently, the Saslauth user was created with quotes in the comment field ("Saslauthd user"). With this update, unnecessary quotes have been removed from the comment field. (BZ#1082564)

* Previously, Cyrus was not able to authenticate against older SASL implementations, which prevented Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 from authenticating to Active Directory (AD) and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 Identity Management (IdM) servers. The change that introduced the problem has been reverted, and Cyrus can now authenticate to AD and IdM servers as expected. (BZ#1154566)

* The support for the non-confidentiality and non-integrity layer of the Generic Security Services (GSS) API was missing. As a consequence, an attempt to look up users on the IBM AIX systems using the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) failed in some cases. With this update, the missing support has been added to the cyrus-sasl library, and the lookup now succeeds. (BZ#1174322)

* Previously, the runtime directory for the saslauthd daemon was unconditionally owned by root. As a consequence, running saslauthd as a non-root user was not possible without complicated workarounds. With this update, the systemd manager creates the directory during run time based on actual settings of the service unit file, and saslauthd can be easily run without root privileges. (BZ#1188065)

Users of cyrus-sasl are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix these bugs.
